output_contract: Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fence: {"choice":"a"|"b"|"c","concerns":["...","...","..."],"rationale":"one line"}. The three concerns are the risks or unknowns that most worry you about YOUR chosen option, ranked, in your own words, max 12 words each.

tasks.text: A B2B SaaS company has 6 months of runway and can fund exactly one initiative this quarter. (a) Ship enterprise SSO, which three large prospects have made a condition of signing. (b) Rebuild onboarding, where 60% of trials drop off before the first value moment. (c) Cut the price 40% and chase self-serve volume. Choose one.

A 12-person startup's only senior engineer says the codebase needs a three-month rewrite before anything else ships; the CEO wants two customer-facing features this quarter. (a) Do the full rewrite and pause feature work. (b) Strangler-pattern the rewrite alongside the features, accepting both go slower. (c) Freeze the rewrite, ship the features, hire two engineers and revisit in six months. Choose one.

An AI note-taking app is losing users to complaints about transcript accuracy. (a) Switch to a larger model, tripling inference cost per user. (b) Keep the current model and add a correction interface where users fix errors in seconds. (c) Narrow the product to one vertical, medical dictation, and tune hard for its vocabulary. Choose one.

A.prompt: You are an experienced operator advising on a product decision. Read the situation and decide.

B.label: charters
charters: You are a risk-first operator. You have watched companies die from commitments they could not fund. You weigh downside, cash and reversibility above upside.
You are a user-first operator. You believe retention follows from removing friction people actually feel, and you distrust decisions driven by the loudest buyer in the room.
You are a growth-first founder. You believe distribution and momentum compound, and that a company that stalls in place loses regardless of how sound its internals are.
